score.doctor_final_text:
Doctor: No fracture, which fits a soft-tissue jersey finger — a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion from the bone. This needs prompt hand-surgeon evaluation since delayed repair worsens outcomes.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon avulsion) of the right ring finger, Leddy-Packer type likely I-II given no bony fragment on X-ray — refer urgently to hand surgery.

dialogue.text: How long has your right ring finger been swollen and painful, and did it start after any injury, cut, or splinter?
It started about 2 days ago when I was playing football. My finger got caught in another player's jersey and he pulled away really hard. It's been swollen and painful ever since.
Was there any visible deformity, or could you bend and straighten the finger normally right after the injury?

Right after it happened, I could still move it a little, but now I can't bend the tip of my finger at all when I try to make a fist. The finger also kind of stays extended even when I'm not trying to move it.
Doctor: That sounds like a "jersey finger" — is the pain and swelling mostly around the last joint near the fingertip, and is there any bruising there?
Yes, the pain and swelling are definitely worst right at that last joint near the tip. There is some bruising there too, and it's pretty tender when I touch it.
Doctor: Can you feel any tenderness or a lump in your palm near the base of that finger, where the tendon may have retracted?
I'm not really sure, let me check... No, I don't feel any obvious lump in my palm. The pain and tenderness are really just at the fingertip joint itself.

Doctor: Understood. I'd like to get an X-ray of the finger to rule out an avulsion fracture at the site of tendon attachment.
